column3: Directly parallels the diseased and hypocritical claim that divine promise is deception.
Sets a boundary against following hypocritical direction, without the trust claim.
Shows crisis exposing speech that diverges from what is in hypocrites' hearts.
Links hypocrisy and diseased hearts with destabilizing public rumor.
Contrasts the opponents' showy arrogance and obstruction with faithful reliance in the same scene.
Shows fabricated religious assurance becoming deception within religion.
Shows hypocrites fearing disclosure of what their hearts conceal.
Sets divine counterplanning against hostile plotting in the immediate battle context.
Supports the powerful and wise divine agency named in 8:49.
Shows diseased hearts and their concealed hostility being brought out.
Places hypocrites within a broader differentiated outcome, but adds little to the verse's claim.
Directly states believers' reliance on Allah amid what befalls them.
Adds the self-reinforcing relation between diseased hearts and lying.
The preceding false assurance and withdrawal sharpen the contrast with genuine trust in 8:49.
Reiterates Allah as mighty and wise without the contested perception or reliance.
Shows diseased hearts acting from fear and later facing what they concealed.
In the same battle setting, locates victory and heart-assurance with Allah, mighty and wise.
Defines believers by growing faith and reliance on their Lord.
In the same passage, attributes the joining of hearts to Allah, mighty and wise.
Adds divine separation of corrupt from good, but not the verse's trust or accusation.
Offers general guidance and return under divine wisdom.
Directly presents reliance on Allah as sufficient amid an ordered divine decree.
Names the distinction between believers and hypocrites but is less specific than earlier cards.
Adds tranquility in believers' hearts and divine forces under wise knowledge.
Shows reassurance, unseen support, and Allah's higher word in adversity.
Adds divine awareness of weakness and battle endurance, without the trust accusation.
Its contrast link marks a boundary rather than positive support for the focus reading.
Connects allegiance to Allah with prevailing, supporting the confidence at issue.
Shows hypocritical promises to allies as false when tested.
General praise of the wise and aware does not materially specify 8:49.
Shows hypocrites finally separated from believers whose light they seek.
Adds reluctance among believers in the immediate battle setting, but no further focus theme.
Names divine might with forgiveness, only loosely related to the closing names.
Shows deviation after clear signs under divine might and wisdom.
General reward for believers adds no distinct understanding of 8:49.
Illustrates deception and its consequence, but in a distant narrative setting.
The legal provision and closing names add no focused link.
Gives the immediate command for steadfast, God-centered conduct in battle.
Rejects false partners under Allah's might and wisdom, with limited focus overlap.
Exposes hypocritical testimony as false despite its outwardly true wording.
General inclusion among the righteous adds no distinct focus evidence.
Calls unsupported mutual promises among wrongdoers deception.
Adds falsehood against Allah and eventual exposure, but not the verse's core contrast.
Adds discernment granted through reverence, countering impaired reading of believers' trust.
General transcendence from false descriptions adds no distinct focus link.
Adds heart reassurance and divine might and wisdom, without the contested reliance.
States the scope of faith and disbelief but does not develop 8:49's contrast.
Adds accountable warning under divine might and wisdom, only indirectly relevant.
Depicts the unstable in-between position associated with hypocrisy.
In the immediate setting, contrasts obedient endurance with internal dispute and failure.
Adds proud opposition and division, but little about deceptive appraisal or trust.
The isolated statement adds no interpretable focus link.
Shows repeated reversal between belief and disbelief, extending divided allegiance.
Exposes hypocritical display and minimal inward remembrance.
General final repayment and recognition of truth adds no distinct focus link.
Adds battle deterrence in the immediate passage, but not the verse's themes.
General assertion of divine strength does not illuminate the focus.
The private estimate of duration lacks a focused connection.
Names punishment for hypocrites without adding their misreading or reliance.
Treats apparent free movement as deceptive, qualifying superficial judgments.
Shows hostile private speech and mischaracterization, only loosely parallel.
Directly declares Allah sufficient for the Prophet and the believing followers.
Contrasts unsupported association with calling upon the mighty, forgiving Allah.
Shows self-serving delay and reaction to loss, indirectly related to crisis conduct.
Presents a believing heart without rancor, only a distant counterpoint to diseased hearts.
Adds personal liability under divine knowledge and wisdom, without the focus contrast.
Uses entrusting language for preserving revelation, but not reliance amid accusation.
The brief location statement has no focused contribution.
Shows people deceived by worldly life in their treatment of religion.
Directly grounds reliance in Allah's sole capacity over harm and mercy.
In the immediate passage, addresses possible betrayal under Allah's knowledge and wisdom.
General description of revelation from the mighty and wise adds little beyond repeated names.
Limits worldly advocacy and asks who can be a guardian before Allah.
Commands separation from mockery and names hypocrites, but lacks the focus contrast.
General firmness and detailing of revelation under wisdom is only remote support.
Connects taking religion as play with worldly deception and absence of any protector apart from Allah.
In the battle context, contrasts reinforcement of believers with fear placed in disbelievers' hearts.
Rejects the calculation that evildoers can escape, with limited focus overlap.
Links faithful worship with replacement of fear by security, relevant to confidence in religion.
General divine power and mercy do not materially develop 8:49.
Warns against being deceived by disbelievers' movement, but remains general.
A rebuke of judgment without a specific connection to the focus themes.
The legal and social directives add no focused contribution.
Shows turning away from divine judgment, only indirectly related to distorted appraisal.
Pairs firm dissociation with reliance, return, and final destination in Allah.
Repeats Allah's might and wisdom without a distinct contextual contribution.
Names diseased and hardened hearts as especially implicated by satanic trial.
Shows the same sign increasing believers' certainty while diseased hearts question it.
Shows diseased hearts becoming visibly paralyzed when battle obligation is specified.
Stresses that entrenched hypocrisy may remain hidden, but adds little after prior cards.
Warns against satanic progression and notes divine purification, only remotely relevant.
General provenance of the Quran from the wise and knowing adds no focused link.
Covenant fidelity is a broad counterpoint to hypocrisy, without direct overlap.
Limits the Messenger as guardian, leaving accountability with the recipient before Allah.
The debt-recording procedure has no focused contribution.
Defers divided-group judgment to Allah, only generally related to divine wisdom.
Household etiquette and heart purity add no focused link.
Moses receiving judgment after flight has no material connection.
The fragment supplies no focused evidence.
Directly joins accepting peace with reliance on the all-hearing, all-knowing Allah.
Introduces those who profess belief while not believing, the core hypocritical disparity behind 8:49.
Frames hypocrisy as attempted deception of Allah and believers, clarifying deceptive religious posture.
Shows a public claim of solidarity paired with a contrary private allegiance.
Uses loss of light for a failed claim to guidance, a parallel to impaired perception.
Describes deafness, muteness, and blindness as a settled inability to return.
Depicts unstable response to light and darkness, paralleling vacillating religious perception.
Makes concealed hostility and speech that reveals it explicit among hostile intimates.
Pairs threatened failure with Allah as guardian and a direct command for believers to rely on Him.
Records suspicion about Allah in crisis and words that conceal what is in hearts.
Grounds victory and defeat in Allah and directly commands believers to rely on Him.
Counters fear-inducing pressure with fear of Allah as the believers' proper orientation.
Shows a claim to belief alongside seeking judgment elsewhere and satanic diversion.
Shows turning away when professed believers are called to Allah and the Messenger for judgment.
Shows an outward profession of obedience followed by contrary private planning.
Treats the hypocrites as a category whose reversal creates a disputed posture among believers.
Shows their wish that believers also disbelieve, sharpening the contrary orientation.
Depicts a group seeking security from both sides while reverting when tested.
Links hypocritical alliance-seeking with a misplaced search for might apart from Allah.
Shows hypocrites waiting on outcomes and claiming affiliation opportunistically with either side.
Supplies the terminal consequence of hypocrisy, without further defining the misreading in 8:49.
Preserves repentance, reform, holding fast to Allah, and sincere religion as a contrary route.
Joins courageous entry in a crisis with the direct command to rely on Allah.
Names hypocrites eager for falsehood and distorted hearing, relevant to corrupted reception.
Frames alliance choice in a way that contextualizes the fear-driven movement of diseased hearts.
Commands believers not to take mockers of religion as allies, sharpening communal boundaries.
Shows people taking devils as guardians while supposing themselves guided.
Shows detachment from signs followed by satanic pursuit and error.
Characterizes hearts, eyes, and ears that fail to apprehend, a broader counterpart to diseased hearts.
Places believers' appeal for help before the divine reinforcement of the battle setting.
Adds divine security, heart-strengthening, and firm footing immediately before 8:49.
Places the battle outcome within a recurring pattern of rejecting Allah's signs.
Names persistent covenant-breaking among those who disbelieve, relevant to unreliable allegiance.
Regulates anticipated betrayal openly, supplying a boundary for trust amid possible treachery.
Answers feared deception after a peace inclination by declaring Allah sufficient support.
Prohibits preferring close kin who favor disbelief, clarifying competing allegiance.
Shows reluctance toward mobilization and preference for worldly life in the campaign context.
Contrasts believers' non-exemption from striving with those seeking to hold back.
Links exemption-seeking with hearts in doubt, hesitation, and confusion.
Shows divine withholding of a group's participation and their being kept among the stay-behinds.
Describes hypocritical participation as producing disorder and seeking to spread trial.
Shows hostile pleasure at believers' hardship and distress at their good.
Records emphatic oaths of belonging that the verse denies.
Gathers male and female hypocrites around evil command, good prevention, and forgetfulness of Allah.
Records hypocritical speech of disbelief after an outward submission and a plotted act.
Shows pleasure in remaining behind and dislike of striving, a crisis-behavior parallel.
Shows a religious construction used for harm, disbelief, division, and waiting for an opponent.
Shows diseased hearts receiving further defilement and dying in disbelief.
Shows evasive looking and departure when a surah is revealed.
Places Noah's resolve and his reliance on Allah before hostile plotting.
Joins belief in Allah with direct reliance in the face of Pharaoh's power.
States reliance on Allah against hostile plotting and grounds it in His encompassing rule.
Pairs practical measures with reliance on Allah and denial of independent control over the outcome.
Has messengers declare reliance on Allah while facing their peoples' resistance.
Makes reliance the proper response for those who seek to rely, amid harm from opponents.
Exposes satanic promise as false and denies that his invitation removes human responsibility.
Denies satanic authority over believers who rely on their Lord.
Contrasts this with satanic authority over those who take him as guardian.
Denies satanic power over Allah's servants and names the Lord as sufficient guardian.
Shows conditional, edge-bound worship collapsing when trial replaces benefit.
Records a claim of belief and obedience followed by turning away.
Shows refusal when the same claimants are called to Allah and the Messenger for judgment.
Directly asks whether their hearts are diseased, doubtful, or afraid of injustice.
Shows a professed believer treating human trial as equivalent to Allah's punishment, a crisis misreading.
Shows disbelievers urging others to follow them and falsely offering to bear the consequences.
Places the confederate crisis in terms of shaken eyes, hearts at throats, and varied thoughts about Allah.
Names the testing and severe shaking of believers immediately before the hypocritical statement in 33:12.
Shows a pretext for withdrawal from the crisis while the homes were not exposed.
Shows readiness for internal betrayal when pressed from every side.
Identifies those who hinder and invite companions away from the struggle.
Shows stinginess toward believers and panic-driven speech when fear arrives.
Shows continued fear of hostile groups even after their departure.
Provides the believing response to the same hostile coalition: recognition, increased faith, and submission.
Shows satanic expectation being confirmed by followers, except for a believing group.
Directly warns that worldly life and the deceiver must not deceive concerning Allah.
Shows evil action made attractive so that it is seen as good, a perception-level counterpart.
Directly asks whether Allah is sufficient for His servant, a close support for the reliance claim.
Shows turning back after guidance when satanic embellishment and false hope intervene.
Records secret obedience to those who dislike revealed guidance.
Shows Allah's ability to identify hypocrites by their marks and the tenor of their speech.
Names hypocrites who hold an evil assumption about Allah and expect a turn of evil.
Records excuses by stay-behinds and exposes the contrary content of their hearts.
Shows the thought that believers would not return, made attractive in hearts, as an evil judgment.
Defines believers by absence of doubt and striving, a clear contrast to crisis hesitation.
Directly combines self-deception, doubt, wishful waiting, and deception concerning Allah among hypocrites.
Demonstrates the falsity of hypocritical promises to leave, obey, and support their allies.
Shows their inward fear of believers and their lack of united hearts.
Challenges the gap between saying and doing, a compact hypocrisy-adjacent principle.
Intensifies the condemnation of saying what one does not do.
Shows hypocrites using oaths as a shield while turning others from Allah's way.
Depicts their impressive appearance alongside fear, suspicion, and hidden enmity.
Places struggle against hypocrites beside struggle against disbelievers, marking their distinct threat.
Questions what force could aid disbelievers apart from the Merciful and calls their condition delusion.
